claims.quote: The sea did something you could feel in your teeth before it gave you a sight to match it: a fold that was not a wave so much as a hinge in the water, a quick, obscene doubling where the Qitaf's bow met a second skin of sea and the two moved for a breath as if to replace one another.
The jagged fold in the water matched the torn diagram I'd smoothed from the wreck log.
When he did, the smudged crosses fell under our course like a second chart: the little dark Xs lined where the sea folded, exactly where my hands felt the deck dip.

The compass needle spent a breath where it had been still, then trembled and wandered like a thirsty thing. Binnacle glass went white and then clear as if someone had exhaled between us and the world. The chronometer on the rail juddered; its second hand missed, caught, and then stuttered on as if time itself had hiccuped.
Rasim's cough cut into the moment like a small bell. He held the wheel with both hands until the veins stood in them; the cough took a bit more from him each time and left him paler around the mouth.
I eased a sheet, shifted a coil of chain to starboard, and told Rasim to steer to the swell with his ear more than his eye.
We compensated with the only things that had never failed us: sail trim, weight, and the small human measures of seamanship.
When he looked my way the amulet at my throat answered: a thin, precise thrum, the sort that sat under the skin and made the bone remember.
The island was near enough now that the fog tasted of it, a metallic salt that could have been anything—iron, old promises, the witches' loom.
Then, a hand's-breadth of wood—salt-soft, heat-scrambled, flecked with old black tar—bobbled against our hull and scraped past.
